exam.title: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (V15)
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite; CompTIA recommends about 12 months of hands-on IT support experience. Practice safe laptop/mobile service, protocols/ports and packet paths, SOHO/Wi-Fi, cables/tools, component compatibility and PC builds, printers, virtualization/cloud responsibility, and controlled hardware/network troubleshooting. Pass 220-1201 and 220-1202 from the same V15 series.

review.notes: All five weighted V15 domains are mapped to compatibility-first implementation, three scenarios, eight safe labs and 40 original checks. Same-version and non-dated estimated-2028 lifecycle boundaries are explicit. All eight URLs are cataloged: six reachable and O'Reilly plus Udemy automation-blocked; none missing or broken. No proprietary objective PDF, PBQs, course labs, or recalled questions are used.

findings.title: Formal method was not clearly separated from tested troubleshooting
findings.evidence: Public version 4.0 document explicitly excludes the formal methodology sequence while retaining six practical troubleshooting objective areas.
findings.recommendation: Keep the method as labeled supporting practice and map all 27 numbered objectives; do not use older course/blog wording as scope authority.
findings.resolution: Keep the method as labeled supporting practice and map all 27 numbered objectives; do not use older course/blog wording as scope authority.

findings.title: Summary-based coverage needed finer networking and hardware detail
findings.evidence: The public full outline includes NetBIOS 137–139, DNS record/mail-authentication concepts, DHCP scopes, display attributes and specific print/maintenance tasks.
findings.recommendation: Add port/service and DNS tables, scope/reservation/exclusion planning, host-service/network types, display and printer explanations, and strengthen 42 answers.
findings.resolution: Add port/service and DNS tables, scope/reservation/exclusion planning, host-service/network types, display and printer explanations, and strengthen 42 answers.

findings.title: Connector shape needed a capability-chain worked example
findings.evidence: USB-IF separates Type-C connectors, data capability, Alt Mode and Power Delivery; USB 2.0 Type-C does not implement the higher-speed/Alt-Mode signal paths.
findings.recommendation: Add dock/cable/power diagnostic comparisons without inferring features from connector shape.
findings.resolution: Add dock/cable/power diagnostic comparisons without inferring features from connector shape.

findings.title: RAID redundancy needed explicit capacity and failure-placement cases
findings.evidence: Traditional RAID 0/1/5/6/10 have different capacity and fault tolerance; RAID 10 survival depends on mirrored-pair membership.
findings.recommendation: Add qualified equal-size-drive calculations and counterexamples for same-pair versus different-pair failures; keep physical controller/rebuild labs proposed.
findings.resolution: Add qualified equal-size-drive calculations and counterexamples for same-pair versus different-pair failures; keep physical controller/rebuild labs proposed.

findings.title: A NAT network label does not prove guest configuration
findings.evidence: The manual WinNAT guide explicitly says the NAT itself does not assign endpoint IP addresses.
findings.recommendation: Explain internal/external/private switch choices separately from guest address, gateway, DNS and access policy; no host network changes executed.
findings.resolution: Explain internal/external/private switch choices separately from guest address, gateway, DNS and access policy; no host network changes executed.

findings.title: Reachability and application acceptance needed concrete evidence
findings.evidence: Socket documentation distinguishes stream/datagram operations; receiving an application rejection is different from failure to reach the endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Run an original bounded loopback protocol over both TCP and UDP, with valid and rejected requests, and state that no remote infrastructure was tested.
findings.resolution: Run an original bounded loopback protocol over both TCP and UDP, with valid and rejected requests, and state that no remote infrastructure was tested.

        Known Subtypes: _printer
        NOTE: The meaning of this service type, though called just "http", actually
        denotes something more precise than just "any data transported using HTTP".
        The DNS-SD service type "http" should only be used to advertise content that:
        * is served over HTTP,
        * can be displayed by "typical" web browser client software, and
        * is intented primarily to be viewed by a human user.
        Of course, the definition of "typical web browser" is subjective, and may
        change over time, but for practical purposes the DNS-SD service type "http"
        can be understood as meaning "human-readable HTML content served over HTTP".
        In some cases other widely-supported content types may also be appropriate,
        such as plain text over HTTP, or JPEG image over HTTP.
        Content types not intented primarily for viewing by a human user, or not
        widely-supported in web browsing clients, should not be advertised as
        DNS-SD service type "http", even if they do happen to be transported over HTTP.
        Such types should be advertised as their own logical service type with their
        own DNS-SD service type, for example, XUL (XML User Interface Language)
        transported over HTTP is advertised explicitly as DNS-SD service type "xul-http".
